skill.name: backend-architect
skill.description: Use backend architecture guidance for feature design, code review, refactoring, and problem diagnosis with hexagonal architecture, DDD, SOLID, clean code, and testing checklists.
skill.summary: Guides backend design, reviews, and refactoring with architecture patterns and quality checklists.
skill.author: Bikach

security_audit.summary: All 115 static findings were reviewed against the cited Markdown content. The weak cryptography, reconnaissance, and Ruby backtick detections are false positives caused by prose or Markdown formatting. One medium semantic risk remains because the skill grants broad Bash access for an architecture-review workflow.

remediation.issue: Broad Bash permission in a guidance-focused skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed-tools when passive review is enough, or require explicit confirmation for every shell command.

remediation.issue: Tool guidance includes shell-oriented commands and linters.
remediation.suggestion: Document an allowlist of read-only commands, such as git diff and grep, and avoid running project scripts without user approval.

content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent guidance when designs grow complex and code quality drifts. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured architecture review, refactoring guidance, and backend checklists.
actual_capabilities: Guides feature design with bounded contexts, ports, adapters, and architecture patterns.
Reviews backend changes by priority with location, impact, and recommended solution.
Detects common code smells such as God Class, Feature Envy, Primitive Obsession, and Long Method.
Validates SOLID principles with focused checklists and remediation guidance.
Uses reference examples for hexagonal structure and bad-versus-good refactoring.
Supports testing and performance review with dedicated checklists.
limitations: It is guidance content, not a runnable framework or code generator by itself.
It depends on the host agent permissions for reading files or running tools.
It does not replace domain decisions from system owners.
Source guidance is primarily written in French.

use_cases.title: Design a Backend Feature
use_cases.description: Plan bounded contexts, ports, adapters, and testing before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find architectural drift, SOLID violations, code smells, and missing tests in backend changes.

use_cases.title: Plan a Refactoring
use_cases.description: Break down risky modules into safer steps with behavior preservation and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Backend Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature design for backend architecture. Identify missing bounded contexts, ports, adapters, and tests. Prioritize findings as P0, P1, and P2.

prompt_templates.title: Find Code Smells
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these backend files for code smells. Focus on God Class, Long Method, Feature Envy, Primitive Obsession, Data Clumps, and Shotgun Surgery.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a refactoring plan for this module. Preserve behavior, reduce coupling, improve SOLID compliance, and include tests for each step.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Hexagonal Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this service against hexagonal architecture and DDD. Check domain isolation, ports, adapters, dependency direction, repositories, use cases, and bounded contexts.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed order creation feature.
output: P0: Separate domain rules from persistence concerns before implementation.
P1: Introduce a repository port and keep adapter mapping outside the use case.
P2: Add unit tests for invariants and integration tests for adapter behavior.

output_examples.input: Analyze a legacy customer service class.
output: The class mixes validation, persistence, notification, and formatting responsibilities.
Extract value objects for email and address data before splitting collaborators.
Add characterization tests before moving behavior into focused services.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for a new payment workflow.
output: Use unit tests for domain decisions and state transitions.
Use adapter integration tests for gateway calls and persistence mapping.
Keep end-to-end tests focused on the highest-value user paths.

best_practices: Provide the feature goal, current directory structure, and key code files before asking for review.
Ask for prioritized feedback and require concrete file or module references.
Run suggested refactors in small steps and validate each step with tests.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad architecture advice without sharing the current boundaries.
Do not apply every pattern when a simpler design already solves the problem.
Do not treat checklist feedback as a substitute for production telemetry.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation and propose examples, but teams should review and test all generated code.

faq.question: Which architecture styles does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on hexagonal architecture, Clean Architecture, DDD, SOLID principles, clean code, and backend testing.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Share files or diffs, then ask for prioritized findings with impact and suggested remediation.

faq.question: Can it run shell commands?
faq.answer: The skill declares Bash, Grep, Glob, and Read tools. Shell command use depends on the host agent and should require confirmation.

faq.question: Is the source content only in French?
faq.answer: The source guidance is primarily French, but prompts and responses can be written in English or French.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the goal, changed files, important constraints, test expectations, and architecture concerns.
